sections.heading: I build the systems that keep an institution running.
sections.body: Operations and administration manager in Dhaka. I look after procurement, projects and people, and I build the tools behind them.
sections.items:
Read the record | #record
Get in touch | #contact

sections.heading: What I am usually asked to do
sections.items:
Put structure where there is none | Procurement procedures, approval flows, KPI frameworks and salary policies, written so that a team can follow them without me in the room.
Replace manual work with a system | Income, expense, inventory and attendance trackers, live dashboards and small web apps, built on tools the team already knows.
Carry a project to the finish | Construction coordination, annual programmes, staff training and fundraising campaigns, planned and delivered with contractors, scholars and volunteers.

sections.heading: On the ground
sections.body: Most of this work happens in rooms and on sites, not on a screen.

sections.heading: The record
sections.body: I keep a journal of what I finish. This page reads it directly, so a new entry in the journal appears here by itself. Select an entry to see how it was done.

I am an operations and administration manager based in Dhaka. For the past three years I have run the working side of Imam Bukhari Trust: procurement, HR, compliance, construction coordination, events, and the systems that hold them together.

I trained as an electronics and telecommunication engineer and then took an MBA in supply chain management. That mix shapes how I work. I look for the process underneath a problem, write it down, and where I can, build a tool so nobody has to do it by hand again.

Outside operations I co-author research on Islamic education, prepare training material, and keep studying the Islamic sciences and Arabic.
